pairs.subject: trust-base
pairs.evidence: lib/foundry/runStore.ts:64 The run store's one JSON decoder casts JSON.parse's unchecked any straight to the caller's T with no validating function, so verdicts.json (store.ts:94) and the catalogue docs (catalogue.ts:262) enter typed code as trust-base members that no directive census counts.

techniques.evidence: lib/foundry/runStore.ts:64 A standard decoder returns the unchecked type and is asserted to T. The technique's cure, decoding into unknown and passing it through one checking function, is absent. Callers include readJson<Verdicts> at store.ts:94, whose verdicts then reach ledger rows (commitPlan.ts:109).

lib/foundry/calibration.ts:47 Grades are stored verdicts and carry a pin (grader_digest), and calibration keeps each pin as its own series (seriesKey, calibration.ts:117), so the pin is compared. But the pin covers only the model name plus prompt/schema data. pipeline/foundry/grade.py grader_digest() hashes grader_parts() (prompts, schemas, enums) and not the import closure, so a change to the scoring code (craft_score/credit), which produces the stored craft score, moves no pin.

pairs.registryProposal: verdict-pins-its-checker assumes the checker is code. For a model-as-grader, the instrument is model weights plus prompts plus scoring code. A worked rule for LLM/vision graders (hash the prompt/schema data AND the scoring module's import closure; pin the model by digest rather than by tag) would make the technique directly usable for grader calibration.
